001package dayplanner;
002
003
004import java.util.Scanner;
005import java.io.InputStream;
006
007
008/**
009 * <p>
010 * Console input helper backed by a {@link Scanner}.
011 * </p>
012 * <p>
013 * Read methods display prompts and generally retry invalid input. The stream
014 * constructor also supports scripted input, such as a
015 * {@code ByteArrayInputStream} in a small example program, which is actually
016 * used in {@link dayplanner.Tester} for scripted input.
017 * </p>
018 * <p>
019 * The goal of this class is to make user input as easy as possible to deal with
020 * in application classes. So, this class does a lot of the heavy lifting for
021 * you.
022 * </p>
023 */
024public class Input {
025    /**
026     * Scanner used for reading lines and tokens from the underlying input stream.
027     */
028    private final Scanner SCANNER;
029
030
031    /**
032     * Constructs an <code>Input</code> instance that reads from the specified
033     * stream.
034     * 
035     * @param stream Source of input.
036     */
037    public Input(InputStream stream) {
038        SCANNER = new Scanner(stream);
039    }
040
041    /**
042     * Constructs an <code>Input</code> instance that reads from standard input
043     * (<code>System.in</code>).
044     */
045    public Input() {
046        this(System.in);
047    }
048
049
050
051    /**
052     * Reads and returns an integer from user input, prompting repeatedly until
053     * valid.
054     * 
055     * @return The next parseable integer. Invalid lines are rejected and requested
056     *         again.
057     */
058    public int readInt() {
059        int input = 0;
060
061        do {
062            System.out.print("(integer) > ");
063
064            String line = null;
065            if (SCANNER.hasNextLine())
066                line = SCANNER.nextLine().trim();
067
068            try {
069                if (line == null || line.isEmpty())
070                    throw new NumberFormatException("Empty input");
071                input = Integer.parseInt(line);
072                break;
073            } catch (NumberFormatException e) {
074                System.out.println("\nInvalid integer. Try again:");
075            }
076        } while (true);
077        
078        System.out.print("\n");
079        return input;
080    }
081
082
083    
084    /**
085     * Reads and returns a trimmed string from user input.
086     * 
087     * @return User input as a <code>String</code>, or <code>null</code> if end of
088     *         input.
089     */
090    public String readString() {
091        System.out.print("(string) > ");
092
093        String input = null;
094        if (SCANNER.hasNextLine())
095            input = SCANNER.nextLine().trim();
096        
097        System.out.print("\n");
098        return input;
099    }
100
101
102
103    /**
104     * <p>
105     * Reads and returns a boolean from user input, prompting repeatedly until
106     * valid.
107     * </p>
108     * <p>
109     * Accepts responses beginning with {@code Y}/{@code y} or {@code N}/{@code n};
110     * characters after the first non-space character do not affect the answer.
111     * </p>
112     * 
113     * @return User input as a boolean.
114     */
115    public boolean readBool() {
116        char input;
117        boolean ret;
118
119        do {
120            System.out.print("(Y/N) > ");
121            
122            String line = null;
123            if (SCANNER.hasNextLine())
124                line = SCANNER.nextLine().trim();
125
126            try {
127                if (line == null || line.isEmpty())
128                    throw new IllegalArgumentException("Input cannot be empty. Try typing Yes or No.");
129
130                input = Character.toUpperCase(line.charAt(0));
131                if (input == 'Y') {
132                    ret = true;
133                    break;
134                } else if (input == 'N') {
135                    ret = false;
136                    break;
137                } else {
138                    throw new IllegalArgumentException("Invalid boolean. Try again; try typing Yes or No.");
139                }
140            } catch (IllegalArgumentException e) {
141                System.out.println("\n" + e.getMessage());
142            }
143        } while (true);
144        
145        System.out.println(" ");
146        return ret;
147    }
148
149
150
151    /**
152     * Parses a string representation of time in YYYY/MM/DD HH:MM format.
153     * 
154     * @param str The string representing a time in YYYY/MM/DD HH:MM format.
155     * @return A valid {@link Time}, or {@code null} for empty or invalid input. For
156     *         example, {@code 2026/09/15 14:30} produces a time value.
157     */
158    public static Time parseTime(String str) {
159        if (str == null || str.trim().isEmpty())
160            return null;
161
162        String[] components = str.trim().split("[/:,\\s]+");
163        if (components.length < 5)
164            return null;
165
166        try {
167            int y = Integer.parseInt(components[0]);
168            int m = Integer.parseInt(components[1]);
169            int d = Integer.parseInt(components[2]);
170            int h = Integer.parseInt(components[3]);
171            int min = Integer.parseInt(components[4]);
172
173            return new Time(y, m, d, h, min);
174        } catch (IllegalArgumentException e) {
175            return null;
176        }
177    }
178
179    /**
180     * Reads and returns a valid <code>Time</code> from user input, prompting
181     * repeatedly until valid.
182     * 
183     * @return A valid {@link Time}; malformed values are explained and requested
184     *         again.
185     */
186    public Time readTime() {
187        do {
188            System.out.print("(YYYY/MM/DD HH:MM) > ");
189            String line = null;
190            if (SCANNER.hasNextLine())
191                line = SCANNER.nextLine().trim();
192
193            if (line == null || line.isEmpty()) {
194                System.out.println("\nTime cannot be empty. Please enter format YYYY/MM/DD HH:MM (e.g. 2026/9/10 17:30). Try again:");
195                continue;
196            }
197
198            // Detailed validation error feedback
199            String[] components = line.split("[/:,\\s]+");
200            if (components.length < 5) {
201                System.out.println("\nInvalid format. Expected: YYYY/MM/DD HH:MM (e.g. 2026/9/10 17:30). Try again:");
202                continue;
203            }
204
205            try {
206                int y = Integer.parseInt(components[0]);
207                int m = Integer.parseInt(components[1]);
208                int d = Integer.parseInt(components[2]);
209                int h = Integer.parseInt(components[3]);
210                int min = Integer.parseInt(components[4]);
211
212                Time parsed = new Time(y, m, d, h, min);
213                System.out.print("\n");
214                return parsed;
215            } catch (NumberFormatException e) {
216                System.out.println("\nTime components must be integers. Try again:");
217            } catch (IllegalArgumentException e) {
218                System.out.println("\nInvalid time: " + e.getMessage() + " Try again:");
219            }
220        } while (true);
221    }
222
223    /**
224     * Reads and returns a command string from user input.
225     * 
226     * @return The next line with leading and trailing whitespace removed.
227     */
228    public String readCommand() {
229        System.out.print("(command) > ");
230
231        String input = null;
232        if (SCANNER.hasNextLine())
233            input = SCANNER.nextLine().trim();
234
235        System.out.print("\n");
236        return input;
237    }
238
239    /**
240     * Prompts the user to press Enter and halts until input is received.
241     */
242    public void pressEnterToContinue() {
243        System.out.println("\nPress enter to continue.");
244        SCANNER.nextLine();
245    }
246}
